title: Recreational, Sacramental and Medical: Why There’s No Clear Delineation Between Recreational and Medical Cannabis.

content_html_sanitized:
The three major drugs in our society (other than caffeine) have a long history of multiple uses.

In Christianity, alcohol was first mentioned when Jesus made water into wine for a wedding party, and it was reportedly primo. Clearly recreational.

The next mention of wine was in a very different context, the “Last Supper”, clearly sacramental.

Finally, when Paul wrote to his protege Timothy, he advised him not to abstain from wine entirely, but to have some for his “occasional infirmities”. Clearly medical.

Cannabis has a long history of medical use, and the American Medical Association even opposed the original 1937 Marihuana Tax Act because of their awareness of that history.

See Medical Marijuana And The Banality of Evil In A San Francisco Courtroom

Of course, it was the recreational use of cannabis by jazz musicians and swarthy outlanders that was the basis of the original prohibition. Much later, it was its use by Rock and Roll musicians, and swarthy outlanders that led to its banning, after the 1937 tax was ruled unconstitutional. That is called “Medical Science”, but please forget about the swarthy outlanders part.

Unfortunately, most people are unaware of the history of the sacramental use of cannabis in the Judeo Christian tradition. My old friend, Chris Bennett, has written a very interesting book about it.

See Kaneh BOSM: THE HIDDEN STORY OF CANNABIS IN THE OLD TESTAMENT

But Christianity had pretty much settled on alcohol, wine in the south and beer in the north.

And the sacramental use of cannabis has even been neglected by modern advocates of psychedelics, who aren’t particularly religious anyway. Do shamans have shaboses? 

It wasn’t until the people who discovered the people who discovered America then discovered that they had also discovered tobacco, which must have been really harmless because people liked it so much.

Finally, a few hundred years later, teen cigarette use has decreased from 70.1 percent in 1991 to 17.8 percent in 2021, an almost fourfold decline.

See DRAMATIC DECLINE IN CIGARETTE USE AMONG U.S. TEENS OVER THREE DECADES

Somehow this happened without arresting 30 million Americans, while cannabis use went up during this time. And we are still arresting over 200,000 Americans a year, with the approval of the medical profession. 

See The Individual Courage and Collective Cowardice of the Medical Profession

What the Europeans didn’t notice was that if you use a whole lot of tobacco, it can be psychedelic, depending on how you use it.

See A multidisciplinary approach to ritual enema scenes on ancient Maya pottery 

And it had other medical uses. 

See If You Drowned In Victorian London There Was A Good Chance You'd Get Tobacco Smoke Up Your Anus

Which is why I took swimming lessons, so if I fall into a canal in Amsterdam…

All of the above is actually context for understanding the continuum between the recreational and medical use of cannabis.

First, although cannabis has been used medically for thousands of years, and perhaps recreationally for even longer, both had been largely forgotten early in the twentieth century when the medical profession was desperately trying to look both scientifically and socially respectable, which it really was not until late in the nineteenth century. 

In fact, they had bled people to death for their health, and they refused to wash their hands before delivering babies, and opposed the use of ether in surgery, because surgeons got paid for being fast. 

Can you say, “Iatrogenic”?

Heroin got its name for being “heroic” for being non addictive.

 “From 1898 through to 1910, diamorphine was marketed under the trademark name Heroin as a non-addictive morphine substitute and cough suppressant.” 

On the other hand, late in the twentieth century, when people with AIDS, suffering from nausea and loss of appetite, remembered that “pot” gave them the “munchies” that was not scientific evidence, so they had to be arrested so it would not send the wrong message to children!

And when the public demanded that the government allow medical access to cannabis, the medical establishment then demanded that they be given control over the process.

The fact is that there never has been a clear demarcation between the recreational and medical use of cannabis, especially for seniors. 

Depressed? Take benzodiazepines! 

Or cannabis?

Aching? Take over the counter drugs! No prescription required! 

Or cannabis?

Can’t sleep? Pharmacological Treatment of Insomnia 

Or cannabis?

In the real world, doctors can’t tell whether your back really hurts, or you really can’t sleep, or if you’re just depressed because you have been lied to all your life by politicians and quacks. 

That’s why there is no clear delineation between the medical and recreational use of cannabis. 

See 8 In 10 Marijuana Consumers Use It As A Substitute For Prescription Drugs, New Survey Finds
